title: Triggers, Refraction, Cut-Outs, Hairlines & Traces
description: Animations that play instead of scrub, glass that refracts the page, type around polygons, pointer-wired line figures, and the tool call as a component.

drops.title: Play on Arrival
drops.description: Cross a line and a normal timed animation starts — no scrubbing, no rewinding with the scrollbar.
drops.concept: Scroll-driven animation binds progress to scroll position, which is not what most reveals actually want. The new pair splits the job: timeline-trigger declares a tripwire on one element, animation-trigger says what the animated element should do when it is crossed. Four bands show four enter/exit action pairs — play-once, replay, play-forwards/play-backwards, and play/pause.
drops.source: utilitybend — CSS animation triggers: playing animations on scroll without scrubbing

interaction.mouse: Scroll through the four bands; the panel reports which path is driving and how many crossings fired.
interaction.click: Drag the enter/exit range sliders to move the tripwire and watch the bands fire earlier or later.
interaction.touch: Scroll works identically; the tuning panel is hidden on small screens.

drops.note: Today's Chromium parses animation-trigger and holds the animation at its first frame but never fires it, so the WAAPI driver always runs — the same actions, guaranteed to fire.

drops.title: Glass That Bends the Page
drops.description: Not a blur: a height profile, a slope, Snell's law, and a per-channel displacement of the live backdrop.
drops.concept: Each glass shape gets a curved rim that flattens into a slab. For every pixel the rim's slope becomes an incidence angle, a view ray is refracted through it at the material's index, and the lateral movement is baked into a displacement map. That map is applied to the backdrop three times at slightly different strengths — one per colour channel — which is where the thin rainbow at the edge comes from. Depth, bezel, IOR and dispersion are all live.
drops.source: tomacco/amazing-glass — liquid glass web components tuned against Apple's own rendering

interaction.mouse: Drag any of the three panes across the page and watch the content bend at their rims.
interaction.click: Material sliders rebuild the displacement maps live.
interaction.touch: Dragging works by touch; panes reflow to the smaller viewport.

drops.note: SVG filters inside backdrop-filter are Chromium-only; elsewhere the frost, tint and rim light still render.

drops.title: Type Around a Hole
drops.description: A line-breaker that treats free space as intervals, so a plate can sit mid-column and the setting closes underneath.
drops.concept: CSS wraps text down one side of a float and stops there — no holes in a column, no closing up again. An engine laying out its own lines asks a narrower question per baseline: which horizontal stretches are empty? The answer can be one interval, two either side of a plate, or none. Words are measured once and cached, lines are justified to the intervals they are given, and the drop cap is simply another reserved rectangle.
drops.source: pmndrs/glyph — typography engine with editorial flow, polygon cut-outs and drop caps

interaction.mouse: Drag any of the three plates; the paragraph re-breaks and re-justifies around it on every move.
interaction.click: Type size, leading, shape padding and drop-cap depth all force a fresh reflow.
interaction.touch: Plates drag by touch; the controls move below the sheet on narrow screens.

drops.title: Figures That Answer Back
drops.description: Isometric line figures that map the pointer onto their own geometry, with neighbours following on a falloff.
drops.concept: Each figure wires the pointer to one specific thing: terrain pillars rise on a radius, the key under the pointer presses while its ring dips by a fraction, and the laptop's lid angle follows on a damped spring that overshoots and settles. Everything is a stroke at a constant CSS width, all three figures share a single animation frame, and the loop stops the moment nothing is moving.
drops.source: lucasmarkes/hairline — isometric line figures that answer the pointer

interaction.mouse: Move the pointer over any figure; each reads a different axis of it.
interaction.click: Intensity, stiffness, damping and falloff sliders retune every figure at once.
interaction.touch: Touch and drag drives the same pointer path; keyboard focus poses a figure for non-pointer users.

drops.title: The Tool Call, as a Component
drops.description: A disclosure with a live timer: one line while it runs, arguments, result, copy and retry only when asked.
drops.concept: Agent output has been a wall of scrolling text for two years. The pattern replacing it is a card: collapsed to a single line with a status dot, a summary and a timer that is genuinely counting, expanding to coloured arguments and a result with a copy action, and offering a retry when a call fails. Above a run of them sits a waterfall of nested bars with tokens and cost, the slowest call marked, and branches that fold into their parent.
drops.source: flohoeller/affectui — tool call card and trace waterfall for agent interfaces

interaction.mouse: Click any card to expand its arguments and result; click a caret in the waterfall to fold a branch.
interaction.click: Replay re-runs the trace, Speed changes the clock, Expand all opens every card, and the failed call offers a retry.
interaction.touch: Everything is tap-driven; the waterfall drops its cost column on narrow screens.
